title: Oven-Roasted Crunchy Peruvian Corned Beef Picarones
description: A twist on traditional Peruvian donuts, made with corned beef, crunchy on the outside and chewy on the inside, perfect for a weeknight dinner. Wok-hei and iron teppan cooking techniques add an authentic touch.
instructions: Preheat the iron teppan or a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, anise seeds, cinnamon, and salt.
Add the corned beef to the dry ingredients and mix until just combined.
Gradually add the eggs and mix until a dough forms.
Cover the dough with plastic wrap and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes and divide it into 8-10 equal pieces.
Roll each piece into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk shape.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. When the oil is hot, add a few of the dough disks and fry until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side.
Transfer the fried donuts to a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Brush the tops with the melted butter and sprinkle with granulated cinnamon.
Place the iron teppan or skillet in the oven and roast at 400°F for 10-12 minutes, or until crispy and golden brown.
While the donuts are roasting, mix together the lime zest and a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
When the donuts are done, remove them from the oven and let them cool for a few minutes.
Drizzle with the lime zest mixture and serve warm.
